description: AI Assistant that reduces the size of your application's Docker Image

summary.one_liner: DockerShrink is a beta, AI-assisted command-line tool that optimizes or generates Dockerfiles and .dockerignore files to reduce Docker image size, currently for Node.js apps only.
summary.what_it_does: The tool analyzes a Node.js project's Docker image definition and applies size-reduction techniques such as multi-stage builds, switching to lighter base images like alpine, and dependency checks. It has two commands: "optimize" improves existing Docker-related files, and "generate" creates new Dockerfile and .dockerignore files for projects that lack them. Output is written to a directory, dockershrink.out by default. AI features are optional for optimize and required for generate, and work with any OpenAI-compatible API endpoint (the README names OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, and Ollama). A --debug flag enables debug logging. The README says the API key is not stored, so it must be supplied on each run.
use_cases: Generating a Dockerfile and .dockerignore for a new Node.js project
Reviewing and optimizing an existing Dockerfile
Using a local Ollama model for Dockerfile optimization
Cutting container storage and transfer costs
how_to_run: cd into your Node.js project root
notable: Combines algorithmic analysis of Docker configs with generative AI suggestions
Works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including local Ollama models
Can generate Dockerfile and .dockerignore from scratch
Ships as a standalone binary, installable via Homebrew
caveats: Beta software; currently supports only Node.js applications
On macOS, the binary must be installed via Homebrew because the compiled binary is not notarized
AI features may incur costs from the LLM provider, and generate requires an API key
